newsitem.title: USA: Medaphis names new CFO, assesses direction.
newsitem.headline: Medaphis names new CFO, assesses direction.

text.p: Medaphis Corp said Wednesday it is considering divesting its Healthcare Recoveries Inc and is assessing alternatives for its BSG Corp.
Medaphis also said Wednesday it named Jerome Baglien chief financial officer.
Medaphis said the alternatives it is assessing for BSG include seeking a buyer, a spin-off, or other alternatives that involve more independence for BSG.
Instead, the company said, it plans to focus on its core business of delivering business management services and information products to healthcare providers.

The company said its 1997 operating plan is driven by five elements: exiting non-core businesses promptly; achieving improved predictability of business results through enhanced management accountability and controls; cutting costs and increasing efficiencies in the core business; singular emphasis on excellence in customer service; implementing cross-selling initiatives.
Medaphis said it also has an agreement with its lenders to restructure its credit facilities, which will initially increase liquidity to $285 million from $250 million.
"1997 will be a year of transition for Medaphis," Chairman and Chief Executive David McDowell said in a statement.
Baglien, who was appointed chief financial officer, succeeds Michael Cote, who resigned to "pursue other business and personal interests," the company said in a statement.
Most recently, Baglien was chief financial officer of Keebler.

The company also said that Patrick McGinnis, currently president of Medaphis Healthcare Information Technology, will be returning to his previously held position of CEO of Healthcare Recoveries, where he plans to lead the company as an independent organization.
The company said it has identified a new president of Healthcare Information, but will not make the announcement until later in the first quarter.
The proposals were announced as the company reported its fourth quarter results, showing a loss of $103.7 million, or $1.45 per share, on revenues of $142.9 million.
The quarter included $138.9 million in restructuring and other charges related to its decision to abandon its re-engineering program and to shut down the Imonics operating unit.
In the prior year's fourth quarter, the company reported a net loss of $1.15 million, or $0.02 per share, on revenues of $144.7 million.
